title: Only 7% Pass This Cambridge Entrance Exam
summary: Explore College Foundations, Patterns & Proof, Scientific Reasoning, Supervision Challenge, The Final Assessment across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: College Foundations, Patterns & Proof, Scientific Reasoning, Supervision Challenge, The Final Assessment. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

Independent entertainment challenge. Not an official Cambridge admissions test and not affiliated with any university.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

cambridge-s1q2.question: A sample has a mass of 2.4 kg. What is that in grams?

cambridge-s1q3.question: Which number is not the cube of a whole number?

cambridge-s1q4.question: A plant grows from 12 cm to 18 cm. What is the percentage increase?

cambridge-s1q5.question: Gear A turns clockwise and meshes with B, which meshes with C. Which way does C turn?

cambridge-s1q6.question: Two otherwise identical plants receive different fertilisers. Which growing conditions should stay the same to make a fair comparison?

cambridge-s2q3.question: A marker starts in the top-left of a 3×3 grid and moves one right, then one down. Where is it?

cambridge-s2q4.question: Which result is strongest evidence for a repeatable effect?

cambridge-s2q7.question: A beaker reading rises from 40 mL to 55 mL after an object is submerged. What volume is displaced?

cambridge-s2q8.question: Which variable is measured as the outcome of an experiment?

cambridge-s3q1.question: A sensor reads 3 units too high. It displays 18. What is the corrected value?

cambridge-s3q2.question: A culture triples every hour. It starts at 4. How many are present after two hours?

cambridge-s3q3.question: Starting at 3, repeat this full rule to get each next term: add 2, then multiply by 2. Which sequence is correct?

cambridge-s3q4.question: A graph rises steadily, then becomes horizontal. What does the horizontal section show?

cambridge-s3q5.question: Which net could fold into a cube?

answers.a3: Four squares in a row, with one above and one below the second square

cambridge-s3q8.question: A claim predicts X. The experiment observes not-X under valid conditions. What is the best response?

cambridge-s4q1.question: A calibrated display adds 4 to the raw value. The raw value doubles from 7 to 14. What will display?

cambridge-s4q2.question: Three readings are 10.2, 10.3 and 15.8. What should be checked first?

answers.a4: Whether 15.8 is an error or unusual observation

cambridge-s4q3.question: Which sample satisfies mass > 5 g and temperature < 20°C?

cambridge-s4q4.question: A square is rotated 180°. Where does its top-left marker finish?

cambridge-s4q5.question: A result differs by 0.2 units across repeated trials. What information is needed before calling that meaningful?

cambridge-s4q7.question: Which description shows reflection rather than rotation?

answers.a1: A left-facing shape flipped to face right across a vertical line

cambridge-s5q1.question: A machine applies ×3, then −2. What output comes from input 6?

cambridge-s5q2.question: Two samples start at 50 g. A loses 12%; B loses 8%. How much heavier is B afterward?

cambridge-s5q3.question: A pattern rotates 90° clockwise, then changes colour. Which operation should be applied first?

cambridge-s5q5.question: A marker moves 2 units north, 3 units east, then 2 units south. Where is it relative to the starting point?

cambridge-s5q7.question: A sensor always reads 2 units above the true value. It currently shows 26. The true value falls by 5. What will the sensor show next?

cambridge-s5q8.question: A model predicts 12, 18 and 24 for three trials. Actual values are 13, 17 and 24. What is the total absolute error?
